prerequisites: Solid programming knowledge in the programming language used in the Programming 1 (I) module.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know specific concepts of a second programming language.
Students can differentiate between the implementation of programming concepts regarding syntax and semantics in different programming languages.
Students are able to write more complex programs in various programming languages and can identify the appropriate programming language for a given task.
Students can present concrete problem solutions in discourse with fellow students and teachers and communicate professionally.

syllabus_topics: Transfer/extension of existing programming concepts to a second programming language
assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded examination types from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer, adhering to the valid study regulations. The ungraded examination is performed as part of the accompanying internship. The composition of the portfolio examination is to be taken from the respective valid study regulations. For graded examinations: written assignments as part of portfolio examinations involve solving tasks for approx. 60-90 minutes per assignment; for exams, see the valid study regulations. For ungraded examinations: experimental work includes approx. 10 experiments in total; regular attendance requires at least 85% presence.
